newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish grains prices static amid limited demand.
newsitem.headline: Spanish grains prices static amid limited demand.

text.p: Spanish cereal prices were unchanged on Wednesday amid little interest from either buyers or sellers, dealers said.
"Demand is pretty much stuck, and as farmers are still holding back stocks, there's just not much activity," said a local trader.
Some farmers have been hoarding crop stores in anticipation of higher prices, dealers said.
Ex-farm feed wheat was quoted at 26,500 pesetas per tonne, milling wheat at 27,500 pesetas, barley at 23,500 pesetas and maize at 24,500 pesetas. Durum was quoted at around 32,000 pesetas per tonne.
Prices of all grains except durum wheat eased on Monday after rain in many parts of Spain last week help offset worries of a smaller than expected harvest.
Current forecasts point to mainly dry and sunny conditions, with some light showers forecast in the southern durum-growing region of Andalusia.
